Federal Parliament
House of Representatives, 2082
Second Session
Meeting Number - 37
Federal
Nepal
Parliament,
Notice - 2
(Brief Minutes of the Meeting Proceedings)
Tuesday, Ashad 30, 2083
The meeting of the House of Representatives commenced today at 11:05 AM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
At the beginning of the meeting, Honourable Members from Nepali Congress, Nepal Communist Party (UML), Nepal Communist Party, Labor Culture Party, and Rastriya Prajatantra Party stood before their seats and requested time to speak. Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker granted time to the following Honourable Members, who then expressed their views on various issues including: the Honourable Prime Minister should withdraw the statement made in the House that Nepal has encroached upon India's border and that the statement should be removed from the parliamentary records; individuals who park vehicles with the intention of causing mental distress in front of government buildings and residences/offices of political leadership should be prosecuted; the practice of hiring contract and daily wage employees through contractors, contrary to the Supreme Court's order, should be immediately reconsidered; traffic rules should be applied equally to everyone, not just the general public; Ganesh Nepali's treatment, which should have been at Kirtipur Burns Hospital, was taken to Bir Hospital; the menace of unauthorized individuals moving around hidden within security perimeters has increased; the government formed on the strength of the 'Janji' movement is oppressing the youth; the government is seeking revenge against those who question it; and other related matters:-
Hon. Ganesh Singh Thagunna
Hon. Jan Bahadur Shahi

Meanwhile, after Honourable Aren Rai finished speaking, Honourable Tika Sangraula raised a point of order. During Honourable Ramesh Kumar Mall's turn to speak, he used the phrase "mobilized by the state" in reference to vehicles parked in various locations, which Honourable Tika Sangraula argued was a violation of Rule 21(d) of the Regulations and demanded it be expunged from the House records. Similarly, after Honourable Nishkal Rai finished speaking, Honourable Santosh Rajwanshi raised a point of order, demanding that the phrases "came climbing the ladder of corpses" used by Honourable Jan Bahadur Shahi and "Government of the Eight" used by Honourable Shiv Shankar Yadav when Honourable Nishkal Rai was speaking be expunged from the House records.
Following this, during the impromptu session that commenced, the following Honourable Members expressed their views on various issues: the death of Vivek Mandal of Sarlahi, who was injured by petrol being sprinkled and set on fire; the need for all parties to unite and move forward for prosperity, democracy, the nation, and nationality; the death of Jayashila Shah of Bheri Municipality, Jajarkot, due to being buried in a landslide; the increasing number of civil servants resigning due to rumors of a 30-year service period or mandatory retirement at age 55, necessitating boosting employee morale; the severe shortage of petroleum products due to disrupted road networks in the Far-East caused by rains, making daily life difficult, requiring government attention; the problem of 12 to 18 hours of daily power outages in Sunsari, affecting students' studies, irrigation facilities, and drinking water, and the need for electricity with the required voltage for irrigation; the incident of suspicious vehicle parking at the gate of the Singha Durbar requiring an impartial investigation and strict action against the culprits; the need for the government to provide immediate relief, rescue, and rehabilitation to those affected by the severe disruption to life in Sayal Rural Municipality, Doti, due to heavy rainfall; the need for the government to provide electricity meters on time to industries in Chitwan to facilitate their operation; the incident of three children drowning in ditches left open in Siraha requiring an impartial investigation and strict action against the culprits, as well as appropriate compensation for the families of the deceased; the need for proper arrangements for fertilizer for farmers; the death of 3 people and injuries to 12 others in a Bolero jeep accident while traveling from Budhgal Municipality to Kedarsyu Rural Municipality in Bajhang on Ashad 27, with arrangements for free treatment for the injured; the need to change the work style for development in Nepal, where work is done for only 8 hours, unlike India and China where work is done 24 hours a day for development and prosperity:-

Thereafter, the Right Honourable Speaker drew the attention of the Government of Nepal to the increasing number of disaster-related incidents such as floods, landslides, and inundation with the onset of this year's monsoon, and the need to arrange for effective disaster preparedness, relief, rescue, and smooth and safe transportation to minimize potential human and physical damage.
Following this, Honourable Yuvraj Dulal, on behalf of the Nepal Communist Party Parliamentary Party, expressed his views on contemporary issues.
Subsequently, during the Special Time that commenced, the following Honourable Members expressed their views:-

Meanwhile, after Honourable Khusbu Oli finished speaking, Honourable Ain Bahadur Mahar raised a point of order, stating that while Honourable Khusbu Oli was speaking, the Honourable Prime Minister and the leader of the ruling party, Honourable Rabi Lamichhane, walked between the speaker, Honourable Member, and the Speaker's chair, which is a violation of Rule 20(ch) of the House of Representatives Regulations. He drew the Speaker's attention to this and demanded action.
Subsequently, Honourable Ain Bahadur Mahar, taking impromptu time, drew the House's attention to death threats he had received from Parajuli Ram and Poorna Bikram Kshetri while protesting against the government.
Thereafter, Honourable Sunil Lampsal, Minister for Physical Infrastructure and Transport, presented his views on issues raised during the impromptu, zero, and special times of the House, stating that approximately 90 percent of grievances related to infrastructure have been addressed through 'Hello Sarkar', laws have been amended for economic reform and development, and the Public Procurement Act has been amended due to the situation where construction work is not completed on time because contractors secure contracts through low bidding, leading to a lack of competition, among other matters.
Meanwhile, while the Honourable Minister was speaking, Honourable Guru Prasad Baral raised a point of order, questioning the Minister's statements that could be considered accusatory and misleading towards MPs, and asking how the amount to be sent to the market in three years would be disbursed. Similarly, after the Honourable Minister finished speaking, Honourable Kavindra Burlakoti raised a point of order, drawing attention to the fact that according to Rule 20(jh) of the Regulations, a minister cannot be interrupted with questions while speaking, which the Minister had done while responding to issues raised during the impromptu, zero, and special times of the House.
Thereafter, on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Honourable Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Sobita Gautam presented the "Annual Report of the Judicial Council FY 2081/082", "Annual Report of the Judicial Service Commission FY 2081/082", and "68th Annual Report of the Public Service Commission (2081/82)" to the House, respectively.
Subsequently, Honourable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle presented a proposal seeking permission to introduce the "Bill to Amend and Repeal Some Nepal Laws Related to Finance, 2083".
Thereafter, the Right Honourable Speaker informed the House that since no notice of objection was received from any Honourable Member regarding the proposal seeking permission to introduce the bill, in accordance with Rule 105 of the House of Representatives Regulations, 2083, permission to introduce the "Bill to Amend and Repeal Some Nepal Laws Related to Finance, 2083" has been granted.
Subsequently, Honourable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle introduced the "Bill to Amend and Repeal Some Nepal Laws Related to Finance, 2083".
Thereafter, the Right Honourable Speaker presented for decision the proposal moved by Honourable Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Shobita Gautam on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah: "That the Bill to Revive the Previous Provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, 2083, be sent to the relevant committee for clause-by-clause discussion." The proposal was unanimously approved.
Subsequently, the Right Honourable Speaker presented for decision the proposal moved by Honourable Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Shobita Gautam on behalf of the Right Honourable Prime Minister Balendra Shah: "That the National Service Bill, 2083, be sent to the relevant committee for clause-by-clause discussion." The proposal was unanimously approved.
Thereafter, the next meeting of the House of Representatives was scheduled to be held on Wednesday, Ashad 31, 2083, at 11:00 AM, and the House was adjourned at 3:30 PM.
P.C. Pandey
Secretary
